mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS declining for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for two consecutive months signals labor market deterioration that precedes corporate earnings contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months indicate broad economic contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both decline > 0.5% MoM for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST and INDPRO both decline > 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 1.0% for three consecutive months increase discount rates and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and rising for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and rising for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% MoM for three consecutive months signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with INDPRO growing > 0.5% MoM for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Consumer spending (RSAFS) falling below 350,000 million dollars for two consecutive months indicates weakening household demand that reduces retail sales expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS < 350,000 million dollars for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% and non-farm payrolls declining below 100,000 jobs for two consecutive months signal severe labor market contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.5% and PAYEMS < 100000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE > 5.5% and PAYEMS < 100,000 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion characterized by GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 2.5% annualized and unemployment (UNRATE) below 5.0% leads to overvaluation and profit-taking, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized and UNRATE < 5.0%.
